==A new direction— server-based Furigana Injector==

  The current version of Furigana Injector is one *fat little add-on*- approximately 15Mb (50Mb+ when unzipped). The code is fine; the dictionary files are the problem. I had hoped future developments might make it possible to shrink dictionary size, but it seems that progression in the natural language parsing community is for the opposite direction. [http://www.kokken.go.jp/lrc/index.php?UniDic%2F%B6%E1%C2%E5%CA%B8%B8%ECUniDic UniDic], the apparent successor to IPADIC, is well over 100Mb in size when unzipped.

  For this reason a server-based text-parsing service seems to be the right path forward. I have concerns about user privacy, but if users are aware that their webpage's text is being processed remotely when they press that furigana button then I think their common-sense will be enough.

  The server was developed, and is used by the Chrome version (0.5~) and the 2.0+ versions for Firefox.

== Functionality that is out of (the current) scope ==

  Never say never, but at this time there are some things Furigana Injector will not provide:

  * *Firefox: No special formatting for text in rubies created by Furigana Injector.* E.g. a lighter colour font for the furigana text. As ruby support is presently provided by the [https://addons.mozilla.org/en-US/firefox/addon/1935 XHTML Ruby Support] or [https://addons.mozilla.org/en-US/firefox/addon/6812 HTML Ruby] extensions setting ruby style in Furigana Injector would clash with their settings.

  This doesn't mean _you_ can't change the ruby layout! The ruby support add-ons have their own options. Open Tools -> Add-ons, and then select the Options button on the "XHTML Ruby Support" or "HTML Ruby" add-on.

  * ~~*Bilingual lookup.* E.g. display the english translations. This is separate to the purely japanese morphology that Furigana Injector provides. Instead the commendable [https://addons.mozilla.org/en-US/firefox/addon/2471 rikaichan] Firefox extension provides this functionality.~~ WWWJDIC lookups over ruby elements is now an option, in version 0.8 for Chrome.

  * *Mouseover functions.* Many users of the Firefox version of Furigana Injector also use the strongly mouseover-based [https://addons.mozilla.org/en-US/firefox/addon/2471 rikaichan]. There would be clashes in the DOM event chain if Furigana Injector tried doing it also. Furthermore the user interface that pops up would become cluttered- at least while these two extensions are not coordinated.
